bookTitle: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.statement: Myth: When the stock market crashes, everyone loses money and panic selling is the only option.. Reality: Protective put structures and dynamic delta/gamma hedging mathematically lock in portfolio floors while converting market panics into liquidity windfalls. Application: Designing convex portfolio insurance that gains explosive value during multi-standard-deviation market crashes.

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.statement: Myth: You can only make money in financial markets if you correctly predict whether prices will rise or fall.. Reality: Time decay (Theta) is a mathematical certainty. Option sellers collect guaranteed premium decay as calendar days elapse in sideways channels. Application: Deploying calendar spreads, iron condors, and covered writes that generate weekly yields without directional market moves.

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.statement: Myth: Leverage is inherently reckless and inevitably leads to margin calls and sudden account blowups.. Reality: Disciplined derivatives contracts allow precise capital allocation: achieving 10x economic exposure while keeping 90% of capital in risk-free interest-bearing cash. Application: Equitizing excess corporate cash flows via index futures without liquidation margin vulnerability.

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.statement: Myth: Option prices are simply set by buyers and sellers bidding randomly like in an eBay auction.. Reality: The volatility surface is a live institutional map of crashophobia, forward supply-demand skew, and tail-risk hedging. Application: Reading implied volatility skew to detect institutional positioning weeks before major macroeconomic announcements.

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.topic: 800 pages of heavy stochastic calculus, partial differential equations, and Greek alphabets.
facts.statement: Reassurance: Hull constructs every concept from first-principles fruit-stand barter agreements, coin flips, and basic algebra before introducing calculus.. Analogy: You do not need to understand automotive thermodynamics to drive a sports car; Hull teaches the visual dashboard and controls first.

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)

facts.topic: The belief that options and futures are zero-sum casino gambling.
facts.statement: Reassurance: Derivatives are the foundational plumbing of global commerce; without them, airlines go bankrupt on oil shocks and farmers lose their life savings.. Analogy: Buying insurance on your home is a derivative contract; Hull teaches you how to insure and monetize financial capital.

sourceCitation.book: Fundamentals of Futures and Options Markets (John C. Hull)
